newsitem.title: RWANDA: Refugees continue to flood back into Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Refugees continue to flood back into Rwanda.

text.p: Tens of thousands of exhausted and hungry Rwandan refugees trekked slowly into Rwanda from eastern Zaire on Sunday in a weary tide of humanity, overrunning aid agency workers trying to reach them.
Rwandan troops apparently abandoned the border checkpoint at the Petite Barriere bottleneck into the border town of Gisenyi when the tide of refugees started moving at first light.
They appeared to have given up the virtually impossible task of checking the refugees' possession bundles.

The increasingly exhausted procession was packed as close as the bundles on their heads would allow, as the line of refugees plodded east in a human stream stretching for at least 30 km (20 miles), witnesses said.

An estimated 200,000 had already crossed through the single open checkpoint into Rwanda since the exodus of exhausted, desperate and hungry people from the refugee camps in eastern Zaire began on Friday.

Children shouted "biscuits, biscuits" at any foreigner seen walking through the crowds. Small groups rested on spare ground off the 12-metre (yard) wide dirt road before rising to their feet and rejoining the moving flood of humanity.

At a small warehouse just behind the border inside Rwanda, workers of the International Committee of the Red Cross struggled to load a thousand children, separated from their parents in the exodus, on to trucks.
But scores of other abandoned children wandered through the wall of people on the road, wailing in terror and clutching small bundles.
The influx had halted during the night, with the refugees huddled in the open along the road, waiting for dawn, when the human tide re-formed.

World Food Programme (WFP) spokesperson Brenda Barton told Reuters a WFP truck had been overwhelmed by desperate refugees when it was carrying a consignment of high-protein biscuits to a distribution point.
"These are desperate people, scrambling for food," she said.
WFP was trying to set up supply dumps along the route of the refugee flood, in order to enable workers to distribute the food in an orderly manner.
Food supplies were also being sent to centres inside Rwanda, where the returning refugees are heading after crossing the border.
